findings.message: Accepted risk with adequate disclosure. The frozen scope remains unchanged and says target construction is excluded, while the implementation and both retained raw grids include creation of the one-element constant target inside the timed loss stage. PD-001 identifies the exact sentence and observed execution, lists both affected grids, assesses the same-arm scalar impact, and records a prospective preconstructed-target requirement. The claim register, execution record, report, project status, and benchmark documentation consistently disclose the mismatch. Retaining rather than rewriting the original and optimized raw grids preserves the preregistered failure and post-outcome history and is the appropriate disposition.

evidence.detail: Preserves the original independent minor finding and required-action alternatives.
PD-001 records protocol text, observed execution, affected grids, impact, disposition, and future correction.
C1 discloses included target creation contrary to the scope sentence.
Execution record repeats mismatch, impact, and retain/disclose/future-fix resolution.
Report labels PD-001, retains measurements, and requires future preconstruction.
Original hypothesis-failing grid remains byte-for-byte retained.
Post-outcome optimized grid remains byte-for-byte retained under the same deviation.

findings.required_action: Do not retroactively modify either raw grid. In a future benchmark version, preconstruct and pass the target before timing, give the revision a new protocol/run identity, and do not transfer old latency values into the revised boundary.

limitations: This was a hash-bound method re-review; no GPU benchmark or reproduction execution was performed.

The original preregistered latency hypothesis remains falsified: original N=8192,k=128 static/EGNN latency is 109.88430699217133/62.60076750186272 ms, ratio 1.7553188463528289. Its peak-memory ratio 0.1408706176972667 passes only memory and cannot rescue latency.

The post-outcome boundary remains explicit: optimization-scope.md was frozen after the failed original grid and diagnostic profile; source identities and grids remain separate; optimized results are descriptive.

Optimized raw values still support C3/C4. At N=8192,k=64, static latency and memory ratios are 0.8493852376158857 and 0.27393681761857375. At k=128 they are 0.4067155168041175 and 0.13768510208547394. Dynamic k=128 ratios are 0.5799317468641675 and 0.1408816250872595.

PD-001 is too small and common across arms to plausibly reverse the large original failure or optimized k=128 crossover, but no separate preconstructed-target grid was run; this is an impact assessment, not measured equivalence.

Inference remains bounded to one synthetic graph, eager FP32, one recorded GPU, prebuilt receiver-regular edges, and a private same-harness EGNN. No accuracy, convergence, public-EGNN fidelity, arbitrary-topology, domain-generalization, or multi-graph-throughput inference is supported.
Twenty synchronized repeats yield within-run medians but no across-process, across-seed, or cross-hardware uncertainty.
Reviewer identity and organizational independence are not authenticated by the runtime; independent=true is an attestation.
